target: High-powered, interactive Modern Horizons-style two-player Limited
status: Curated research library; imported into a generated runtime catalog for prompt reference selection

scope.excluded: Planeswalkers and other unsupported card types; Aura and Equipment are covered within their card types.

methodology.facts: Fetched from the public Scryfall API and pinned to specific printing IDs; type and rarity checked mechanically. Summaries are paraphrases, not complete rules text.
methodology.judgments: Editorial judgments for the stated support and cost context, not Scryfall or Wizards ratings. Constructed bans are evidence about that format and shell, not automatic Limited verdicts.
methodology.rarity: Uses the selected printing, not first printing or cheapest/latest version. VMA Tolarian Academy is a digital draft reprint at mythic.
methodology.comparison: Match role, cost, color commitment, and support after rarity/type. A row is not a universal linear ranking between dissimilar effects.
methodology.metrics: No numerical win-rate claims. The attempted dated 17Lands request returned null win rates and was not used.

entries.name: Writhing Chrysalis
entries.effect_summary: Four mana buys a reach body, two Spawn on casting, and permanent growth whenever another Eldrazi is sacrificed.
entries.rationale: Above the desired common ceiling: it supplies its own fuel, grows while refunding mana, and improves sharply in multiples. Treat this as a common outlier to avoid normalizing, not the baseline for every four-drop.
entries.context_and_costs: Eldrazi/Spawn support makes the ceiling higher; the two included Spawn already turn it into a 4/5 and generate two mana when sacrificed.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Eldrazi Repurposer
entries.effect_summary: A three-mana 3/3 makes one Spawn when cast and another when it dies.
entries.rationale: A useful body plus immediate and deferred resources is the desired common floor for a supported midgame role. There is value even when the main creature trades.
entries.context_and_costs: Spawn sacrifice, ramp, and death synergies add value. The cast trigger also supplies a Spawn if the creature spell is countered.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Hill Giant
entries.effect_summary: Four mana for a vanilla 3/3.
entries.rationale: Below the target: no immediate resource, evasion, resilience, or synergy compensates for spending a midgame turn. This is a deliberately obvious lower bound.
entries.context_and_costs: Creature-type bonuses could improve it, but do not justify this baseline in an ordinary supported deck.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Sprout Swarm
entries.effect_summary: Creates a Saproling; convoke helps pay its two-mana cost and optional three-mana buyback.
entries.rationale: Too strong as a frequent common in a creature-rich environment: the output helps fund later casts while buyback preserves the spell. It can take over stalled games without drawing more engine pieces.
entries.context_and_costs: Conditional ceiling: needs bodies or spare mana and is vulnerable to counters and board resets. It is not automatically infinite.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Galvanic Discharge
entries.effect_summary: One red mana supplies three energy, then spends any amount of available energy as damage to a creature or planeswalker.
entries.rationale: This is the desired efficiency: three damage for one mana without needing prior setup, with a relevant resource interface. Do not weaken it just because it is common.
entries.context_and_costs: Additional energy can increase damage; spending less can bank energy. It cannot damage players.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Healing Salve
entries.effect_summary: One white mana either gains three life or prevents the next three damage to a target that turn.
entries.rationale: Usually too little lasting value for spending a card. A dedicated combat save can work, but the generic common slot should offer broader protection, replacement, or offensive use.
entries.context_and_costs: Damage-based combat can make prevention useful; this is a weak default, not a claim it never wins a combat.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Treasure Cruise
entries.effect_summary: Draws three cards; graveyard cards can pay the seven generic mana through delve.
entries.rationale: Too strong when routine play reliably makes this cost one blue mana: a large resource refill with almost no tempo loss. The printed eight mana is not its effective price in a stocked graveyard.
entries.context_and_costs: Conditional ceiling: without self-mill, cheap spells, or a developed graveyard it is expensive. Delve consumes resources other cards may need.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Malevolent Rumble
entries.effect_summary: For two mana, selects a permanent from the top four, mills the rest, and creates a Spawn.
entries.rationale: A strong common should perform useful jobs together: find a needed resource, stock the graveyard, and leave a body or future mana. This is a concrete generation anchor.
entries.context_and_costs: Can miss on a permanent-light deck. Permanent density and graveyard synergies matter; this is not unconditional draw-two.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Divination
entries.effect_summary: Three mana at sorcery speed draws two cards.
entries.rationale: Below our premium spell-slot target: it replaces itself and gains one card but supplies no board, selection, discount, or later reuse. Prefer a meaningful second job at this cost.
entries.context_and_costs: Still playable when the format is slow or card draw is scarce. A near-floor reference, not an intrinsically bad Magic card.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Pestilence
entries.effect_summary: A four-mana enchantment converts each black mana into damage to every creature and player; it expires if the battlefield has no creatures at the end step.
entries.rationale: Above the common ceiling in a small-creature format: repeatable board control and player damage concentrate too much of the game in one widely available engine.
entries.context_and_costs: Needs black mana, life to spend, and often a durable creature. High toughness, enchantment removal, and the end-step condition provide counterplay.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Witness Protection
entries.effect_summary: One-mana Aura removes a creature's abilities and makes it a 1/1.
entries.rationale: Appropriate strong common interaction: a tiny mana commitment substantially answers a threat while leaving the opponent a body and possible escape routes.
entries.context_and_costs: It is not hard removal. Enchantment removal, bounce, and sacrifice can undo or exploit the remaining creature.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Asha's Favor
entries.effect_summary: Three-mana Aura grants flying, first strike, and vigilance without increasing size.
entries.rationale: Too much card and tempo exposure for an enhancement with no replacement or immediate body. A removal response can erase the investment.
entries.context_and_costs: A protected large creature or Aura-specific deck improves it; assess those supports rather than assuming every keyword package is valuable.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Cranial Plating
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana Equipment adds power equal to artifact count; equip costs one, with a two-black instant attachment option.
entries.rationale: Above our common payoff ceiling when artifacts are plentiful: it translates cheap permanents and artifact lands into large evasive damage at very low attachment cost.
entries.context_and_costs: Conditional ceiling: count actual artifacts, evasive carriers, and removal. A low-artifact set should not reject its descendants by name alone.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Lembas
entries.effect_summary: Two mana gives scry and a card immediately; later two mana and sacrifice gain life, and the artifact shuffles back when it dies.
entries.rationale: A useful artifact replaces itself before asking for synergy. The later sacrifice is optional utility, not the sole reward for spending the original card.
entries.context_and_costs: The later life costs two more mana. Artifact entry, sacrifice, and Food support raise its value; shuffling it back is not an immediate extra card.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

printing.set_name: The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth

entries.name: Golden Urn
entries.effect_summary: One-mana artifact accumulates upkeep counters and can be tapped and sacrificed for that much life.
entries.rationale: Spends a card for slow life gain without affecting the board or replacing itself. Cheapness alone does not rescue an effect with so little return.
entries.context_and_costs: Artifact-count support supplies some value, but stronger cantrip artifacts can usually fill that role.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Seat of the Synod
entries.effect_summary: An artifact land that enters untapped and produces blue mana.
entries.rationale: Too efficient when artifact count is a major resource: a normal land drop also discounts affinity, grows payoffs, and supplies sacrifice material without a tempo charge.
entries.context_and_costs: Conditional ceiling: ordinary in decks without artifact rewards; vulnerable to artifact removal. Compare with the tapped Bridge, not with a spell that consumes mana.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Silverbluff Bridge
entries.effect_summary: An indestructible artifact land that enters tapped and produces blue or red.
entries.rationale: A good common synergy land: fixes two colors and supports artifacts, with a real entry-tempo cost. The cost keeps the extra resource type from being free.
entries.context_and_costs: Still inspect affinity and indestructible interactions. Strong common fixing is not license to make every land untapped.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Shimmering Grotto
entries.effect_summary: Produces colorless normally; producing a chosen color requires paying an additional mana.
entries.rationale: Below the intended routine fixing floor: each colored activation ties up an extra mana source and disrupts the curve. It can rescue a splash but should not be the premium fixer.
entries.context_and_costs: Five-color flexibility has value; compare total mana available after filtering, not just number of colors listed.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Amped Raptor
entries.effect_summary: A two-mana 2/1 first striker supplies energy and, when cast from hand, can use energy to cast the next revealed nonland card.
entries.rationale: Conditional upper boundary: with many cheap hits or surplus energy it bundles a creature, resource production, and a free spell into an explosive early turn. Do not reproduce reliable high-end hits for two mana.
entries.context_and_costs: In an ordinary draft curve it can miss on an unaffordable spell. Its Modern ban is corroboration of an optimized energy shell, not proof that every Limited copy is excessive.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Flametongue Yearling
entries.effect_summary: Two red mana buys a 2/1 that deals its power to a creature on entry; each two-mana kicker adds a counter.
entries.rationale: A real uncommon power anchor: body plus removal at two mana, with scaling when drawn late. Strong two-for-ones belong in the target environment.
entries.context_and_costs: Double red constrains casting. The damage target is mandatory and can be your own creature if no opponent creature is available.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Air Elemental
entries.effect_summary: Five mana buys a 4/4 flyer with no other ability.
entries.rationale: Below the intended premium uncommon finisher: it does not refund a card, answer a threat, or protect the investment. This is a useful near-floor comparison for bland expensive flyers.
entries.context_and_costs: Flying still wins games. In a slower or flyer-light environment it can be good; the verdict concerns our stronger target.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Mana Drain
entries.effect_summary: A two-blue counterspell supplies colorless mana equal to the countered spell's mana value at the next main phase.
entries.rationale: Above the desired interaction ceiling: a full answer also finances a much earlier threat. Increasing rarity changes frequency but does not remove the tempo swing.
entries.context_and_costs: Requires a relevant opposing spell, double blue, and a way to use the temporary colorless mana. Its uncommon and mythic printings demonstrate why rarity alone is not a power scale.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Counterspell
entries.effect_summary: Two blue mana counters a spell without a type restriction.
entries.rationale: This is a fair high-powered uncommon answer. Full interaction at two mana is allowed; do not add a weak tax or a four-mana price to make it feel safe.
entries.context_and_costs: Needs double blue and mana held open; cannot remove a permanent already in play.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Frazzle
entries.effect_summary: Four mana counters a nonblue spell.
entries.rationale: A four-mana answer with a color exclusion loses the key efficiency that makes countermagic useful. Its restriction does not buy a compensating upside.
entries.context_and_costs: Blue-light opponents improve coverage, but not its tempo cost.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Channel
entries.effect_summary: Two green mana enables paying life for colorless mana during the turn.
entries.rationale: Above the upper bound with expensive generic-cost payoffs: it can bypass most of the mana curve immediately. Moving it from uncommon to mythic does not make that play pattern fair.
entries.context_and_costs: Requires payoff cards and enough life. An empty hand or colored-only costs limit it; do not invent a combo without identifying the payoff.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Lingering Souls
entries.effect_summary: Three mana creates two flying Spirits; a later two-mana flashback makes two more.
entries.rationale: A strong uncommon provides an independently useful first cast and a meaningful second resource. Two evasive bodies now and two later is the right ambition for token pressure.
entries.context_and_costs: Full output costs five mana across two casts and access to black for flashback. Graveyard hate and sweepers remain relevant.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Ransack
entries.effect_summary: Four mana rearranges the top five cards of a chosen player’s library between top and bottom.
entries.rationale: Spends a card and a full midgame turn without drawing, answering a permanent, or creating a body. Selection needs a better rate or actual resource return.
entries.context_and_costs: Can manipulate an opponent’s draws or support top-deck payoffs; those uses must justify losing a card and tempo.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Land Tax
entries.effect_summary: A one-mana enchantment can repeatedly find up to three basic lands at upkeep when an opponent has more lands.
entries.rationale: Conditional upper boundary for cheap engines: repeated three-card refills can secure every land drop and fuel discard or hand-conversion effects with minimal mana investment.
entries.context_and_costs: It finds lands into hand, not the battlefield. Needs the land-count condition, basics, and preferably a way to use excess lands; it can be inactive when ahead.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Goblin Bombardment
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana enchantment converts sacrificed creatures into damage to any target without a mana activation cost.
entries.rationale: A strong, desirable build-around: every activation consumes a real creature. Free activation alone is not a reason to nerf a finite-resource engine.
entries.context_and_costs: Check token density and recursion. If a concrete cheap loop produces unlimited creatures, the package can cross the ceiling.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Honden of Cleansing Fire
entries.effect_summary: Four-mana Shrine gains two life per controlled Shrine at upkeep.
entries.rationale: As a lone engine, it has no immediate board impact and only a small recurring reward. This is the same failure mode as the generated four-mana life-gain enchantment.
entries.context_and_costs: Shrine density changes the evaluation substantially. This weak verdict assumes no dedicated multi-Shrine package.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Skullclamp
entries.effect_summary: One-mana Equipment gives a power bonus and toughness penalty; equipped creatures dying draw two cards. Equip costs one.
entries.rationale: Above the ceiling: one-toughness tokens become very cheap two-card refills, and normal removal also feeds the engine. Common fodder makes this accessible without elaborate setup.
entries.context_and_costs: Count one mana per equip and a consumed creature. Those costs remain far too small when tokens are abundant.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Barbed Spike
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana Equipment arrives attached to a 1/1 flying Thopter, adds one power, and later equips for two.
entries.rationale: A two-mana 2/1 flyer up front plus reusable equipment later is an excellent uncommon baseline. The first body pays for the development turn.
entries.context_and_costs: The token and Equipment are separate permanents; count both artifact entry triggers, but do not double-count the same creature's power.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Angel's Feather
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana artifact gains one life when a player casts a white spell.
entries.rationale: No board effect, card return, or serious payoff for its setup. Increasing the number of trigger opportunities does not automatically make a weak reward worthwhile.
entries.context_and_costs: Life-gain payoffs can help, but prefer enablers that also attack, block, or replace themselves.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Strip Mine
entries.effect_summary: A land produces colorless mana or sacrifices itself to destroy any land.
entries.rationale: Above our utility-land ceiling: a land slot can erase an opponent's only basic of a color, and recursion can lock development. Basics do not provide a safe escape.
entries.context_and_costs: One-for-one land trading has a real cost. Recursion and low-land aggressive decks make it most dangerous; the verdict is about the desired play experience as well as efficiency.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Ghost Quarter
entries.effect_summary: A colorless land can sacrifice to destroy a land, whose controller may find a basic replacement.
entries.rationale: A reasonable safety valve: it answers a problematic land while usually preserving the opponent's ability to play. The replacement is an intentional cost, not useless generosity.
entries.context_and_costs: Needs actual troublesome lands to justify the slot. Repeated activations can exhaust basics; inspect recursion and basic counts.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Terminal Moraine
entries.effect_summary: A colorless land requires two mana, tapping, and sacrifice to find a tapped basic.
entries.rationale: Below the fixing target because the conversion ties up the land plus two other mana and delays the replacement. Low immediate cost hides substantial tempo loss.
entries.context_and_costs: It offers late flexibility. Its weakness is the full conversion cost, not an inability to produce mana.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Nadu, Winged Wisdom
entries.effect_summary: A three-mana flying creature grants creatures target-triggered land-or-card value, limited separately for each creature each turn.
entries.rationale: Above the ceiling with repeatable cheap targeting: per-creature limits and new creatures do not meaningfully bound the engine. Evaluate the entire trigger network, not just the word twice.
entries.context_and_costs: The documented constructed failure used Shuko or Outrider en-Kor, then more complex loops. A draft set without targeting enablers is a different context.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Psychic Frog
entries.effect_summary: A two-mana creature draws on player or planeswalker combat damage, grows by discarding cards, and gains flying by exiling graveyard cards.
entries.rationale: An ambitious but appropriate rare target for a supported blue-black lane: pressure, resource conversion, and card advantage on a cheap interactive body.
entries.context_and_costs: Needs combat connection; growth consumes cards and flying consumes graveyard material. Its Legacy ban does not automatically make the design an invalid high-powered Limited reference.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Wood Elemental
entries.effect_summary: A four-mana creature requires sacrificing untapped Forests on entry; those sacrifices determine its size.
entries.rationale: An obvious lower bound: development is paid twice, first in mana and then in lands, for a body with no compensating impact or protection.
entries.context_and_costs: Land-sacrifice synergies rarely recover the immediate tempo loss. Do not treat printed mana as the full cost.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Ancestral Recall
entries.effect_summary: One blue mana lets a target player draw three cards.
entries.rationale: Far above the ceiling: two net cards for a single mana with no setup, leaving the rest of the turn available for development or interaction.
entries.context_and_costs: This is a deliberately extreme upper bound, not a close comparison for every draw spell.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Force of Negation
entries.effect_summary: Counters and exiles a noncreature spell; outside your turn, a blue card can be exiled instead of paying three mana.
entries.rationale: A suitable rare efficiency anchor: zero-mana defense is allowed when it costs another card, has a timing gate, and misses creatures.
entries.context_and_costs: Free use spends two cards to answer one. Evaluate blue-card density and the set's noncreature threats; it is not a universally efficient two-for-one.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Pale Moon
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana instant makes nonbasic lands produce only colorless mana for the rest of the turn.
entries.rationale: A narrow one-turn inconvenience is not enough for a premium rare interaction slot. It neither removes a threat nor reliably denies the opponent a useful action.
entries.context_and_costs: An opponent can often float colored mana in response, and basics are unaffected. Nonbasic-heavy combo matchups are special cases.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Balance
entries.effect_summary: Two mana reduces players' lands, hands, and creatures to the smallest respective counts through sacrifice and discard.
entries.rationale: Above the ceiling when a deck converts resources into unaffected permanents: the nominal symmetry can become a cheap one-sided reset.
entries.context_and_costs: Requires tracking what each player actually loses. Artifact/enchantment-heavy boards and emptied hands break the symmetry; it is not literally a one-sided spell.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Damn
entries.role: spot removal with a sweeper mode
entries.effect_summary: Two black mana destroys a creature; four-mana overload instead destroys every creature.
entries.rationale: A desirable rare combines efficient early interaction with a major late board option. Flexibility creates rare value without making the baseline weak.
entries.context_and_costs: The single-target and overload modes require different colored commitments. The sweeper also destroys your creatures.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Morality Shift
entries.effect_summary: Seven mana exchanges its controller's library and graveyard.
entries.rationale: Too little immediate board or resource access for a normal expensive spell slot. It asks for another payoff after consuming most of a turn.
entries.context_and_costs: Dedicated graveyard wins can exploit it. Such a package must exist in the actual set before this is credited as a finisher.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Opposition
entries.effect_summary: Four-mana enchantment lets creatures tap to tap an artifact, creature, or land.
entries.rationale: Above our ceiling in a token-rich environment: spare creatures can deny mana before main phases as well as clear blockers, turning a board lead into a soft lock.
entries.context_and_costs: Needs a creature board and can be attacked by removal or sweepers. Tapping only blockers without land denial would be a different design.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Bitterblossom
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana enchantment creates a flying Faerie each upkeep at the cost of one life.
entries.rationale: A real rare engine can accumulate evasive material cheaply. It is acceptable to gain repeated value when the first token is delayed and life loss creates a race.
entries.context_and_costs: No immediate body, continued life loss, and enchantment answers matter. Sacrifice or tribal packages can push it higher.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Conjured Currency
entries.effect_summary: Six-mana enchantment can trade control of itself for an eligible permanent at each upkeep of its current controller.
entries.rationale: Below target: no entry impact, a full-turn delay, and the opponent receives the same exchange tool. It does not reliably secure the resource it appears to steal.
entries.context_and_costs: Ownership restrictions affect eligible targets. A carefully engineered board can improve it, but ordinary use is slow and unreliable.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Umezawa's Jitte
entries.effect_summary: Two-mana Equipment gains counters from combat damage; counters provide removal, pump, or life. Equip costs two.
entries.rationale: Above our combat ceiling: the first connection finances future removal and makes subsequent combat increasingly unfavorable. Multiple resource modes snowball from normal attacks or blocks.
entries.context_and_costs: Full initial investment is four mana plus a creature. Killing the carrier or artifact remains possible, but the accumulated counters make racing and small creatures much worse.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Nettlecyst
entries.effect_summary: Three-mana living-weapon Equipment supplies a Germ and scales its bonus with controlled artifacts and enchantments; later equip costs two.
entries.rationale: A strong rare build-around supplies its own body and rewards the deck's ordinary permanents. This is a much better expensive Equipment pattern than paying twice before obtaining any creature.
entries.context_and_costs: Count the Equipment itself; Germ dies if its final toughness is zero. Actual artifact/enchantment density controls the ceiling.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Jayemdae Tome
entries.effect_summary: Four mana to cast, then four mana and tapping to draw each card.
entries.rationale: The first card costs eight total mana and only replaces the Tome. Repeatability does not excuse a huge initial tempo deficit in this environment.
entries.context_and_costs: A very slow control game can eventually repay the investment. Compare that timetable to immediate cantrips and draw engines attached to threats.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Tolarian Academy
entries.effect_summary: A legendary land taps for blue mana equal to the number of controlled artifacts.
entries.rationale: Above the ceiling with cheap artifacts: a land drop produces multiple mana without an activation investment. Artifact tokens can accelerate the engine further.
entries.context_and_costs: Conditional ceiling: it produces nothing without artifacts. Rare and mythic printings are both shown; neither rarity makes a dense artifact shell safe.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Prismatic Vista
entries.effect_summary: A land sacrifices with one life to find a basic land, which enters untapped.
entries.rationale: Appropriate premium fixing: any basic color on demand without a tempo delay, paid for with life and restricted to basic targets.
entries.context_and_costs: Does not fetch duals merely because they have basic land types. Landfall and graveyard support add value; basics must be available.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Wintermoon Mesa
entries.effect_summary: Enters tapped, produces colorless, and can spend two mana plus sacrifice to tap two lands.
entries.rationale: Weak premium land: an entry penalty and no fixing buy only temporary disruption with another activation cost and loss of the land.
entries.context_and_costs: Specific denial strategies can use it. A routine draft deck should prefer colored sources or more reliable utility.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Uro, Titan of Nature's Wrath
entries.effect_summary: Three mana gains life, draws, and can put a land into play; escape later retains a 6/6 that repeats the value when attacking.
entries.rationale: Conditional upper boundary: cheap stabilization and acceleration lead into a recurring threat, making one-for-one answers struggle to catch up. This is an engine package, not just a large creature.
entries.context_and_costs: Requires escape mana and five other graveyard cards for the persistent body. Graveyard hate and exile change its resilience; do not omit those costs.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Archon of Cruelty
entries.effect_summary: An eight-mana 6/6 flyer creates a sacrifice, discard, life swing, and card draw on entry and attack.
entries.rationale: This is appropriate ambition for eight mana: immediate recovery plus a real closing threat. Do not flatten its payoff to a bare large body because the effect looks dramatic.
entries.context_and_costs: The opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker rather than a chosen target. Cheap reanimation or repeated blink can move this beyond the hard-cast reference context.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Sphinx Sovereign
entries.effect_summary: An eight-mana 6/6 flyer gains three life at your end step if untapped, otherwise makes opponents lose three life.
entries.rationale: Below the eight-mana mythic target: no entry card or removal swing, difficult colors, and most value requires surviving until a later step.
entries.context_and_costs: Can stabilize against flyers and eventually race. Compare immediate payoff and colored requirements with Archon rather than body size alone.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Mana Drain
entries.effect_summary: A two-blue counterspell supplies colorless mana equal to the countered spell's mana value at the next main phase.
entries.rationale: Above the desired interaction ceiling: a full answer also finances a much earlier threat. Increasing rarity changes frequency but does not remove the tempo swing.
entries.context_and_costs: Requires a relevant opposing spell, double blue, and a way to use the temporary colorless mana. Its uncommon and mythic printings demonstrate why rarity alone is not a power scale.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Magma Opus
entries.role: expensive flexible board and card swing
entries.effect_summary: Eight mana combines divided damage, tapping permanents, a 4/4 token, and two cards; discarding it for two mana instead makes a Treasure.
entries.rationale: A suitable mythic spell offers several concrete returns when expensive and an early use when stuck in hand. This is the right scale for a late-game resource swing.
entries.context_and_costs: Costs eight at instant speed; the early Treasure mode spends the card. Casting from the graveyard cheaply would require separate package review.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Stunning Reversal
entries.effect_summary: Four-mana instant replaces the next game loss that turn with drawing seven and setting life to one, then exiles itself.
entries.rationale: Weak default mythic slot: no development or ordinary interaction, must be held for a narrow crisis, and often leaves the player exposed at one life.
entries.context_and_costs: A special alternate-loss combo or protection plan can improve it. Do not credit that package when absent.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Channel
entries.effect_summary: Two green mana enables paying life for colorless mana during the turn.
entries.rationale: Above the upper bound with expensive generic-cost payoffs: it can bypass most of the mana curve immediately. Moving it from uncommon to mythic does not make that play pattern fair.
entries.context_and_costs: Requires payoff cards and enough life. An empty hand or colored-only costs limit it; do not invent a combo without identifying the payoff.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Echo of Eons
entries.effect_summary: Six-mana spell shuffles hands and graveyards into libraries and draws seven for everyone; flashback costs three.
entries.rationale: A suitable high-powered build-around when its graveyard mode is deliberately supported: a meaningful hand reset at an attractive alternate price, with real symmetry and sequencing decisions.
entries.context_and_costs: Needs discard or mill to access the cheaper mode. Also refills the opponent; free discard and fast mana can make the package excessive. Not a general-purpose baseline draw spell.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Archangel's Light
entries.role: expensive life gain and graveyard reset
entries.effect_summary: Eight mana gains two life per graveyard card, then shuffles that graveyard into the library.
entries.rationale: Too little board or usable card impact for an eight-mana mythic. A large life total can delay losing without providing a way to recover or win.
entries.context_and_costs: Life-gain payoffs and decking can matter; without them, compare it directly with a finisher that also removes, draws, or supplies bodies.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Necropotence
entries.effect_summary: A three-black enchantment trades life for cards arriving at the end step, while skipping normal draws and exiling discarded cards.
entries.rationale: Above our sustained-card-advantage ceiling: many cards can be purchased for life without further mana, rapidly overwhelming ordinary exchanges.
entries.context_and_costs: Triple black, delayed access, hand size, skipped draws, and pressure on life are real constraints. They do not make life a substitute for a meaningful ongoing mana cost.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: The Meathook Massacre
entries.effect_summary: An X-cost enchantment shrinks all creatures on entry and then turns deaths into life swings.
entries.rationale: A strong mythic should affect the board immediately and leave a coherent engine. The sweeper scales with actual mana spent; the remaining triggers need creatures to die.
entries.context_and_costs: The shrink effect hits your creatures too. Small-creature density and token sacrifice can raise its ceiling; do not automatically label every death trigger excessive.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Cast Through Time
entries.effect_summary: Seven-mana enchantment gives its controller's instants and sorceries rebound.
entries.rationale: Below target as an ordinary engine: spends seven mana and a card without changing the board, then requires another spell and time to realize the payoff.
entries.context_and_costs: A deck with abundant mana and strong spells can exploit it. The label is about its unsupported floor and deployment timetable.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Mana Crypt
entries.effect_summary: Zero-mana artifact taps for two colorless; upkeep coin flips can deal three damage to its controller.
entries.rationale: Above the ceiling: repeatable two-mana acceleration without a mana investment skips early curve stages. Random life loss does not reliably repay that tempo advantage.
entries.context_and_costs: Long games make the damage relevant. It still accelerates any deck with generic costs and needs very little synergy.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Wurmcoil Engine
entries.effect_summary: Six-mana 6/6 has deathtouch and lifelink; dying leaves two 3/3 tokens, each inheriting one ability.
entries.rationale: A strong mythic can dominate combat, stabilize life, and leave material after destruction. That is a suitable payoff for six mana in a powerful environment.
entries.context_and_costs: Colorless access makes this a high-end target, not an average six-drop. Exile, bounce, theft, and artifact answers differ from ordinary destruction.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Alhammarret's Archive
entries.effect_summary: Five-mana artifact doubles life gain and most card draws, excluding the first draw in the draw step.
entries.rationale: Below target without a substantial support package: no body, entry value, or benefit to the ordinary first draw. Another effect must produce the resources it doubles.
entries.context_and_costs: With many repeatable draw or life-gain effects it can become powerful. Count those sources before assigning either verdict.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Tolarian Academy
entries.effect_summary: A legendary land taps for blue mana equal to the number of controlled artifacts.
entries.rationale: Above the ceiling with cheap artifacts: a land drop produces multiple mana without an activation investment. Artifact tokens can accelerate the engine further.
entries.context_and_costs: Conditional ceiling: it produces nothing without artifacts. Rare and mythic printings are both shown; neither rarity makes a dense artifact shell safe.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Cavern of Souls
entries.effect_summary: A land names a creature type; it produces colorless normally or any color for that type's creatures, which become uncounterable.
entries.rationale: A useful mythic land reference when tribes overlap: untapped fixing plus specialized protection without producing extra mana or winning by itself.
entries.context_and_costs: Only the colored-mana mode carries the creature-type restriction and uncounterability. It cannot pay arbitrary colored noncreature costs; no supported tribe means this is the wrong target.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

entries.name: Maze's End
entries.effect_summary: A tapped land produces colorless; a three-mana activation returns it to hand, searches for a Gate, and checks for ten differently named Gates.
entries.rationale: Too weak in our current unsupported Gate context: slow fixing and an unreachable alternate victory do not justify a mythic slot.
entries.context_and_costs: A deliberate ten-Gate environment changes the verdict. It is a support-mismatch example, not evidence that alternate-win lands must always be weak.
entries.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Refurbished Familiar
supplemental.effect_summary: Four-mana 2/1 flyer with artifact discounts and an entry discard effect that draws instead when the opponent cannot discard.
supplemental.rationale: A cheap supported common can supply evasion and immediate card advantage. Compare the expected discounted cost, not just the printed four.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Strong target only with declared artifact density. Artifact lands and plentiful tokens can make one-mana casts routine; check that ceiling.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Thraben Charm
supplemental.effect_summary: Two-mana instant chooses creature-count damage, enchantment destruction, or graveyard exile.
supplemental.rationale: Modes make an answer relevant in more matchups. Common interaction can be flexible and efficient without needing extra drawback clauses.
supplemental.context_and_costs: The damage mode depends on your board and can fail to kill through removal. The other modes do not require creatures.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Unholy Heat
supplemental.effect_summary: One red mana deals two damage to a creature or planeswalker, increasing to six with four graveyard card types.
supplemental.rationale: Two damage is already useful. Ordinary deck construction can unlock a major payoff, instead of unlocking mere playability.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Delirium requires actual type diversity and graveyard access. Do not assume six damage is always available on turn one.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Thraben Inspector
supplemental.effect_summary: One white mana makes a 1/2 and a Clue.
supplemental.rationale: An inexpensive enabler should leave material immediately and a useful later option. This is a good floor for small value creatures.
supplemental.context_and_costs: The Clue costs two more mana to draw. It is not a free immediate cantrip; artifact and token synergies add separate value.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Faithless Looting
supplemental.effect_summary: One red mana draws two and discards two; a three-mana flashback repeats it.
supplemental.rationale: Card disadvantage can be worthwhile when the spell is very cheap and actively enables graveyard plans. Do not ban every draw/discard pattern after the weak two-mana sample.
supplemental.context_and_costs: The first cast loses one net card. It needs valuable selection or discarded-card use, and flashback costs real mana.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Abiding Grace
supplemental.effect_summary: Three-mana enchantment offers one life or returns a one-mana creature at each of your end steps.
supplemental.rationale: This is a substantial engine that can pay off on the casting turn. The attractive mode returns a real creature, not just a little life.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Requires enough one-drops, trades, and sacrifice outlets. Judge repeated entry/death effects; the life mode is the fallback.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Static Prison
supplemental.effect_summary: One-mana enchantment exiles an opposing nonland permanent, supplies two energy, and needs energy at each first main phase to remain.
supplemental.rationale: A one-mana broad answer can be strong with a genuine duration constraint. The card comes with its first maintenance payments.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Additional energy extends the removal. Without it, the threat returns; counting this as permanent unconditional exile misprices it.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Persist
supplemental.effect_summary: Two mana reanimates a nonlegendary creature with a minus-one counter.
supplemental.rationale: High-powered recovery can return a meaningful body directly at an aggressive rate. Five mana merely to put an artifact into hand is nowhere close.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Requires a creature in the graveyard. Large entry effects such as Archon of Cruelty change the acceptable package; this is not permission for arbitrary early cheat targets.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Tireless Tracker
supplemental.effect_summary: Three-mana 3/2 makes Clues from landfall and gains counters when Clues are sacrificed.
supplemental.rationale: A threat can link routine land drops, delayed cards, and permanent growth. This is a coherent rare engine rather than a weak body with unrelated flavor text.
supplemental.context_and_costs: No guaranteed entry Clue unless a land can follow it. Each ordinary Clue activation costs two; do not count all future cards as immediate.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Solitude
supplemental.role: removal creature with a costly free mode
supplemental.effect_summary: Five-mana 3/2 with flash and lifelink exiles another creature for life compensation; pitching a white card can evoke it.
supplemental.rationale: Efficient interaction attached to a useful body is appropriate at mythic. A free defensive mode may deliberately trade card economy for tempo.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Evoke normally sacrifices Solitude, so pitching spends two cards for the removal. Blink can evade that sacrifice; inspect the exact package before approving it.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Ornithopter of Paradise
supplemental.effect_summary: Two-mana 0/2 artifact flyer taps for any color.
supplemental.rationale: Two mana can provide both a blocker and flexible acceleration. Creature vulnerability and summoning sickness are meaningful costs, not reasons to add more taxes.
supplemental.context_and_costs: It cannot tap for mana immediately without haste. Artifact synergies improve it; board wipes also remove the acceleration.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Worn Powerstone
supplemental.effect_summary: Three-mana artifact enters tapped and later produces two colorless mana per tap.
supplemental.rationale: A three-mana ramp investment should create a meaningful jump. Compare a rock’s future output and entry delay with its casting cost.
supplemental.context_and_costs: No fixing and no mana on the entry turn. Multiple copies or untap effects require reviewing how early expensive threats arrive.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Bonesplitter
supplemental.effect_summary: One-mana Equipment adds two power and equips for one.
supplemental.rationale: A small combat bonus needs a small combined investment: two total mana for the first equipped attacker, then one to move it.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Supplies no body or card replacement. Evasion and token density matter, and removing the carrier can create a tempo loss.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Basking Broodscale
supplemental.effect_summary: A two-mana 2/2 can adapt for two mana and makes a Spawn whenever it receives one or more counters.
supplemental.rationale: An appealing supported common on its own, but it becomes a concrete unlimited loop with Sadistic Glee. This is a package warning, not a blanket ban on counters.
supplemental.context_and_costs: With Glee attached, sacrifice a Spawn: Glee adds a counter to Broodscale, which makes the next Spawn. Each repetition produces colorless mana; an initial Spawn or paid adapt starts it.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending

supplemental.name: Sadistic Glee
supplemental.effect_summary: One-mana Aura gives its enchanted creature a counter whenever a creature dies.
supplemental.rationale: Cheap individually modest enablers can remove the limits on another card. Review the loop with Broodscale rather than adding arbitrary once-per-turn text to every sacrifice card.
supplemental.context_and_costs: Needs Broodscale, the Aura, and a starting death or Spawn; removal can disrupt the chain. Unlimited colorless mana needs a sink to win immediately, while the creature also grows without bound.
supplemental.judgment_status: editorial; human calibration and draft playtesting pending
